    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Reflection.Representation, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Reflecting a representation at a sink #

    For a sink i of a quiver Q -- a vertex no arrow leaves -- the Bernstein-Gelfand-Ponomarev construction turns a representation M of Q into a representation of the reflected quiver LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.Reflect Q i, in which every arrow at i points the other way. Away from i nothing changes; at i the vector space Mᵢ is replaced by the kernel of the map

    ⨁_{a : b ⟶ i} M_b → Mᵢ

    that sums the actions of the arrows into i, and each reversed arrow acts by the corresponding coordinate projection out of that kernel. This file builds that representation and computes its dimension vector, and bundles the construction as a functor on representations.

    The content of the computation is that on dimension vectors the construction realizes the simple reflection sᵢ of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Reflection.DimensionVector, provided the summing map is surjective: the reflected space at i then has dimension ∑_b #(b ⟶ i) · dim M_b - dim Mᵢ, which is exactly sᵢ applied to the dimension vector of M, because a sink has no outgoing arrow. Surjectivity is the honest hypothesis here and it is not automatic: it fails exactly the way LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_not_surjective records, for a representation concentrated at i whose space at i is nontrivial, of which the vertex simple Sᵢ is the example. The reflection has zero vertex space at i in this boundary case, by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.subsingleton_reflectRep_obj_self; in particular, it kills the vertex simple Sᵢ.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum: the map ⨁_{a : b ⟶ i} M_b → Mᵢ summing the arrows into a vertex, defined at every vertex of every representation, whose range contains the image of every arrow into that vertex (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.map_toPath_mem_range_incomingSum).
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep: the reflection C⁺ᵢ M of a representation at a sink i, a representation of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.Reflect Q i.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor: the BGP reflection functor at a sink.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_single: the incoming sum of a family supported at one arrow is the action of that arrow.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_naturality: the incoming sum is natural in the representation.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep_obj_self and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep_obj_of_ne: the vertex spaces of C⁺ᵢ M.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep_map_reflectArrow and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep_map_reflectArrowOfNeOfNe: the action of a reversed arrow, by a coordinate projection out of the kernel, and of an arrow away from i, unchanged.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor_obj: the functor sends M to LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep M, so the whole reflectRep interface computes its objects.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor_map_app_self_apply and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor_map_app_of_ne: the action of reflection on morphisms.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor_additive: the reflection functor is additive.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep_of_ne and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep_self_add: the dimension vector of C⁺ᵢ M, away from i and at i.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep: dim (C⁺ᵢ M) = sᵢ (dim M) when the summing map is surjective.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_not_surjective: that surjectivity fails for a representation concentrated at i with nontrivial space there, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.subsingleton_reflectRep_obj_self: the reflected space at i vanishes under the same source-vanishing hypothesis. Together they describe the vertex simple Sᵢ, the boundary case of the previous result.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.forall_subsingleton_reflectRep_obj and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isZero_reflectRep: a representation concentrated at the sink reflects to the zero representation, the same boundary case read at every vertex and on the whole reflection.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.finiteDimensional_reflectRep_obj: reflection preserves finite-dimensionality of the vertex spaces.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.nonempty_iso_of_isZero_away_of_linearEquiv and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.nonempty_iso_of_dimVector_eq_of_forall_subsingleton: two representations concentrated at the same sink are isomorphic as soon as their vertex spaces there are, respectively as soon as their dimension vectors agree.

    Implementation notes #

    The vertex spaces branch on equality with i, so they are written with an if and decided classically; no DecidableEq Q instance therefore appears in the interface of the construction, exactly as for LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.simpleRep. Only the statements naming LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexPreReflection assume DecidableEq Q, because Pi.single needs one.

    The vertex spaces, the prefunctor that LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep lifts, and the kernel maps underlying the action on morphisms are private. The reflectRep_obj_*, reflectRep_map_*, reflectionFunctor_obj, and reflectionFunctor_map_app_* theorems provide the interface downstream files should use. The body of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor is not exposed outside this module, so reflectionFunctor_obj cannot be proved by rfl where it is stated; it restates a private unfolding lemma. A vertex space of a functor object is therefore computed by reflectionFunctor_obj followed by the matching reflectRep_obj_* result, and that composite is exactly the transport appearing in the reflectionFunctor_map_app_* statements.

    The arrows of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.Reflect Q i are given by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.reflectHom, which is again an if on equality with i, so an arrow of the reflected quiver is a cast of an arrow of Q: LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.reflectArrow and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.reflectArrowOfNeOfNe name the two casts, and the computation rules for the action are stated on them. Both branches at i that a general vertex would allow are impossible at a sink -- the reflected quiver has no arrow into i and i carries no loop -- and the definition discharges them from LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.IsSink.

    The universes are constrained the least the construction allows: the vertex spaces of M are taken in max v w x for the vertex universe v, the arrow universe w and an arbitrary x, because the reflected space at i is cut out of a product indexed by the arrows into i, which lives in max v w together with the vertex spaces. The universe of the field is unconstrained.

    A vertex i : Q is used below as an object of the free category CategoryTheory.Paths Q, which is Q itself only by unfolding a semireducible definition; as in the neighbouring files, the CategoryTheory.Paths.of annotations record that identification where a proof needs it.

    References #

    This implements the reflection at a sink of the reflection functors of Layer 4 of TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations/README.md. See Bernstein--Gelfand--Ponomarev, Coxeter functors and Gabriel's theorem, and Derksen--Weyman, An Introduction to Quiver Representations, Ch. 2.

    The sum of the arrows into a vertex #

    source
    noncomputable def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) (i : Q) :
    ((e : (b : Q) × (b ⟶ i)) → ↑(M.obj e.fst)) →ₗ[k] ↑(M.obj i)

    The sum of the arrows into a vertex. For a representation M of a finite quiver and a vertex i, this is the linear map ⨁_{a : b ⟶ i} M_b → Mᵢ sending a family of vectors, indexed by the arrows into i, to the sum of their images under the corresponding arrows. Its kernel is the vector space that LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep puts at i. It is LinearMap.lsum applied to the actions of the arrows into i; the decidable equality that combinator needs is supplied classically, so none appears in the interface.

    No hypothesis on i is imposed: the map is defined at every vertex, and it is the reflection that needs i to be a sink.

      The reflected representation #

      QuiverRep k (Quiver.Reflect Q i)

      The reflection of a representation at a sink i: the representation C⁺ᵢ M of the reflected quiver LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.Reflect Q i that agrees with M away from i, puts the kernel of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum at i, and lets each reversed arrow act by the matching coordinate projection out of that kernel.

        A reversed arrow acts by a coordinate projection. The arrow i ⟶ b of the reflected quiver coming from an arrow e : b ⟶ i of Q sends an element of the kernel at i to its coordinate at e. The source b of such an arrow is automatically distinct from i, since a sink carries no loop.

        theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_naturality {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] {M N : QuiverRep k Q} (η : M ⟶ N) (i : Q) (f : (e : (b : Q) × (b ⟶ i)) → ↑(M.obj e.fst)) :

        The sum of the arrows into a vertex is natural in the representation. Applying a morphism η coordinatewise to a family indexed by the arrows into i and then summing is the same as summing first and applying η at i; it is the naturality of η along those arrows, read off one coordinate at a time.

        The components of the reflected morphism are transports of components of the original one, so every identity about them is an identity of the original conjugated by eqToHom. The general transport API is in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Categorical.EqToHom, including the conjugation rules for the identities, compositions, and sums used to construct the reflection functor.

        CategoryTheory.Functor (QuiverRep k Q) (QuiverRep k (Quiver.Reflect Q i))

          If every vertex space at the source of an arrow into i vanishes, then the sum of the arrows into i is the zero map.

          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_not_surjective {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) (i : Q) (h : ∀ (b : Q) (a : b ⟶ i), Subsingleton ↑(M.obj b)) (hne : Nontrivial ↑(M.obj i)) :
          ¬Function.Surjective ⇑(incomingSum M i)

          The sum of the arrows into i need not be onto. It fails to be whenever every vertex space at the source of an arrow into i vanishes while the space at i does not, which is what the vertex simple Sᵢ does at a sink: no arrow into a sink is a loop, so Sᵢ vanishes at every source of such an arrow. This is why the surjectivity hypothesis of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep cannot be dropped.

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.subsingleton_reflectRep_obj_self {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (h : ∀ (b : Q) (a : b ⟶ i), Subsingleton ↑(M.obj b)) :
          Subsingleton ↑((reflectRep M hi).obj i)

          The reflected space at the sink vanishes when all incoming sources vanish. If every vertex space at the source of an arrow into i vanishes, then the reflected space at i vanishes too. In particular, this is the sink-vertex computation showing that reflection annihilates the vertex simple Sᵢ.

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.forall_subsingleton_reflectRep_obj {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (h : ∀ (a : Q), a ≠ i → Subsingleton ↑(M.obj a)) (j : Q) :
          Subsingleton ↑((reflectRep M hi).obj j)

          Reflection annihilates a representation concentrated at the sink. If every vertex space of M away from i vanishes, then the reflection is the zero representation: at i by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.subsingleton_reflectRep_obj_self, since no arrow into a sink is a loop, and away from i because the vertex space is unchanged there. This is the boundary case in which reflection does not act by the simple reflection on dimension vectors -- for an indecomposable representation it is the vertex simple Sᵢ, which LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_not_surjective describes -- and it is what makes a composite of reflections vanish once one of its stages does.

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.isZero_reflectRep {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (h : ∀ (a : Q), a ≠ i → Subsingleton ↑(M.obj a)) :
          CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (reflectRep M hi)

          Reflection annihilates a representation concentrated at the sink, read on the whole reflection: LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.forall_subsingleton_reflectRep_obj says every vertex space of the reflection vanishes, and a representation with vanishing vertex spaces is a zero object.

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.finiteDimensional_reflectRep_obj {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (h : ∀ (a : Q), FiniteDimensional k ↑(M.obj a)) (j : Q) :
          FiniteDimensional k ↑((reflectRep M hi).obj j)

          Reflection preserves finite-dimensionality. The reflected space at the sink is a subspace of a finite product of vertex spaces of M, and away from the sink the vertex spaces are those of M. This is what carries the finite-dimensionality hypothesis of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep through a sequence of reflections.

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep_self_eq_zero {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (h : ∀ (b : Q) (a : b ⟶ i), Subsingleton ↑(M.obj b)) :
          dimVector (reflectRep M hi) i = 0

          If every source of an arrow into the sink vanishes, the reflected dimension at the sink is zero.

          Comparing two representations concentrated at the same sink #

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.nonempty_iso_of_isZero_away_of_linearEquiv {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {M N : QuiverRep k Q} {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (hM : ∀ (a : Q), a ≠ i → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (M.obj a)) (hN : ∀ (a : Q), a ≠ i → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (N.obj a)) (e : ↑(M.obj ((CategoryTheory.Paths.of Q).obj i)) ≃ₗ[k] ↑(N.obj ((CategoryTheory.Paths.of Q).obj i))) :
          Nonempty (M ≅ N)

          Two representations vanishing away from a sink are isomorphic as soon as their vertex spaces at that sink are. Every component away from i is a map between zero objects, and there is no naturality condition to check at i, since no arrow leaves a sink.

          source
          theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.nonempty_iso_of_dimVector_eq_of_forall_subsingleton {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {M N : QuiverRep k Q} {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (hsub : ∀ (a : Q), a ≠ i → Subsingleton ↑(M.obj a)) (hfdM : FiniteDimensional k ↑(M.obj ((CategoryTheory.Paths.of Q).obj i))) (hfdN : IsFinDim k Q N) (hd : dimVector M = dimVector N) :
          Nonempty (M ≅ N)

          A representation concentrated at a sink is isomorphic to every finite-dimensional representation with the same dimension vector. Equality of dimension vectors makes the comparison representation vanish wherever M does, and matches the two vertex spaces at the sink. Only the vertex space of M at the sink is asked to be finite-dimensional, since M is a subsingleton everywhere else; N is asked for it at every vertex, to read a vanishing dimension vector there as a vanishing vertex space.
